purpose: The product's navigation rail: a 240px panel that collapses to a 48px icon strip, peeks open on hover, and carries nested groups, flyouts and badges. Built on the SDK's SideNavBar.

useInstead.when: you want a shell with no design-system dependency
useInstead.use: @faclon-labs/app-shell — do you want a shell, or do you want THIS shell?

useInstead.when: you are below the mobile breakpoint
useInstead.use: AppNavDrawer, which wraps this one — it renders the same rail inside a Drawer

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for the iosense rail. Where it is silent, say so rather than borrowing a rule from the SDK's own SideNavBar guard — this component deliberately overrides several of its behaviours.
decision.beforeTheRules: There are THREE states, not two: pinned open, peeked open, and collapsed. Pinned is a click and moves the page; peeked is a hover and floats over it. Conflating them is the mistake this component was rewritten to avoid.

rules.then: own `isPinned` in the host and pass it down; the rail never stores it
rules.because: the top bar owns the toggle, and a control that hides a panel cannot live inside that panel — collapsed there are 48px and nowhere to put it

rules.if: you are tempted to let the SDK handle the hover peek
rules.then: do not — this component strips the SDK's `data-hovered` in BOTH states and drives the peek itself
rules.because: the SDK sets that attribute inside its own DOM, where React cannot see it. During an SDK-driven peek the component still believed it was a 48px strip while the user looked at a 240px panel: tooltips fired on readable labels, nested groups opened flyouts beside an already-wide panel, and the organisation name stayed hidden

rules.if: you need a rule that applies while the rail is visually open
rules.because: a peek reports as expanded precisely so every existing expanded rule applies unchanged; `isPinned` is false during a peek and any rule using it will be wrong

rules.then: expect a flyout when collapsed and an inline sub-list when open
rules.because: a 48px strip has no room for a nested list, so the collapsed rail hands off to a Popover — and only one flyout is open at a time, because fds Popovers do not join a floating tree and nothing else would close the previous one

rules.if: you want a count or a status word on a row
rules.then: use `badge: { kind: 'count', value, tone }` for numbers and `{ kind: 'word', label, tone }` for text
rules.because: the two render as different components — a Counter and a Badge — and the split is what keeps a number from being styled as a status

rules.then: render AppNavDrawer instead and pass `isPinned` so the rail is always expanded inside it
rules.because: the SDK's own mobile mode was disabled here (`mobileBreakpoint={0}`) — its drawer state lives in the provider with no controlled prop, so the top bar outside could never open it

constraints: The collapse control is NOT in this component. It lives in the top bar.
`theme-overrides.css` must be loaded, and loaded AFTER the SDK's stylesheets. The rail's footprint, its pinned width and its hover shadow all live there.

The rail's own motion is retuned to 360ms by overriding --fds-duration-moderate on `.app-sidenav-theme`. Footprint, panel and menu-button width all animate on that one token, so overriding a single rule instead would desync them.

defaults.railTheme: 'Dark' in this app; 'Light' is the SDK default (the Classic theme)

accessibility.keyboard: Tab reaches every row. Expand triggers are buttons; navigation rows are links. Focus entering a collapsed rail peeks it open so the labels are readable — without that, a keyboard user gets sixteen unlabelled glyphs.
accessibility.aria: The current row carries aria-current="page". Expandable rows carry aria-expanded and an aria-controls that resolves. Collapsed, the parent row stands in for whichever child is current, or the strip would mark nothing at all.
accessibility.notes: Tooltips appear ONLY when a label is unreadable — the 48px strip, or an expanded label truncated by an ellipsis. Never when the text is right there. Since hovering a collapsed row now peeks the rail open, the collapsed-rail tooltip is in practice reserved for truncation.

composition.childrenContract: None. The nav tree is defined inside this component. `workspace` is the only content slot — the organisation row in the header.
composition.notes: The nav rows are currently hardcoded here rather than passed as data. That is a known difference from @faclon-labs/app-shell and is the first thing to change if this needs to serve more than one product.

antiPatterns.dont: Keying behaviour on `isPinned` to mean 'the rail is open'
antiPatterns.do: Key it on the derived open state, or on data-state="expanded" in CSS
antiPatterns.why: isPinned is false during a hover peek, so every such rule is wrong for exactly the case the peek exists to serve

antiPatterns.dont: Letting the SDK's own hover expand the rail
antiPatterns.do: Keep `data-hovered` stripped and drive the peek in React
antiPatterns.why: React cannot see the SDK's attribute, so the component and the screen disagree — and the open/close delays become decorative

antiPatterns.dont: Putting a collapse button inside the rail
antiPatterns.do: Keep it in the top bar
antiPatterns.why: collapsed there are 48px; the button had to be duplicated as a row to stay reachable, and two controls for one state is worse than one in fixed chrome

antiPatterns.dont: Shipping without theme-overrides.css, or loading it before the SDK
antiPatterns.why: the SDK injects component CSS at load; loaded earlier, the overrides lose and the rail's footprint and pinned width are wrong

antiPatterns.dont: Showing a tooltip on every rail row
antiPatterns.do: Let the component decide — it shows one only when the label is hidden or clipped
antiPatterns.why: a tooltip repeating a label the user can already read is noise, and several can end up stacked at once

incorrect.why: isPinned is false during a hover peek, when the label is plainly visible — ask the component, not the pin state
the peek must be owned in React; the SDK's attribute is invisible to the component that has to react to it
